title: The coronation of Charlemagne
subject: histoire
description: On Christmas Day 800, in Rome, Pope Leo III places a crown on Charlemagne's head. The West finds an emperor, and Europe a lasting model.

hero.hook: Christmas 800: a Frankish king becomes emperor, and Europe changes century.

blocks.text: On **December 25, 800**, in Saint Peter's Basilica in Rome, Pope **Leo III** places a crown on the head of **Charles**, king of the Franks. This gesture claims to restore the Roman Empire which had disappeared in the West since **476**.

It's not just a ceremony. It is the birth of an ambition: a Latin Christian empire, distinct from Byzantium (the Eastern Roman Empire), which lays the administrative and cultural foundations of continental Europe.

**Charlemagne** inherits the Frankish kingdom in **768**. After his brother's death, he conquers relentlessly. Thirty years of wars against the **Saxons**, Germanic peoples of present-day Germany, including forced conversion. In **774**, he overthrew the [[Avars]] kingdom of Northern Italy. He subdued Bavaria, crushed the [[Lombard]], nomadic riders of the Danube, and tempted Spain: the ambush of (**778**), a pass in the Pyrenees, entered the legend. [[Roncesvalles]]
At its peak, the empire covered approximately **1.1 million km²**. Too vast to hold by the sword alone. Charles must invent another way of governing.
Charlemagne was approximately **1.84 m**, an exceptional height at a time when the male average was around **1.65 m**.

To hold the empire, Charlemagne relies on , local governors, and , inspectors sent in pairs to control the provinces. In Aachen, its capital, , an English scholar, directs the palace school. We restore Latin, we train clerics, we invent the **Caroline writing**, readable everywhere. [[Counts]] [[The missi dominici]] [[Alcuin of York]]

Monasteries copy ancient texts. Economically,  replaces the too rare gold: a stable currency for daily commerce. It's the **Carolingian Renaissance**: less artistic splendor than order and useful knowledge. [[Silver denarius]]
For his laws to be understood, Charlemagne demanded that they be read aloud to the people, on market days or after mass.

In **799**, Leo III, attacked in Rome, took refuge with Charles. The king restored it. On Christmas Day, the Pope crowned him **“Emperor of the Romans”**. According to his biographer Eginhard, Charles would have been embarrassed: by placing the crown himself, the pope suggests that power comes from the Church.

In Constantinople, capital of Byzantium, there are cries of usurpation. For them, there is only one Roman emperor. Charlemagne creates a second pole. The Latin West asserts its independence. The idea of ​​ was born, which would last for centuries. [[The Holy Roman Empire]]

sections.title: A broken empire, a living idea

blocks.text: After **814**, the unit does not hold. In **843**, the Treaty of Verdun divides the empire between the grandsons of Charlemagne: France in the west, Germany in the east, and a disputed territory in the center. The local power of the lords gains ground. But the counties, writing, currency and the imperial dream survive.
The Imperial title will last until **1806**. Charlemagne became the “Father of Europe”: not because his empire held, but because he gave the West a first great common framework.

On **December 25, 800**, Charlemagne restores the Empire in the West. Divided from **843**, this project nevertheless leaves Europe with its first tools of unity: administration, writing, currency and imperial idea.
